title: Embedded runtime consumption SKUs and SLA PRD
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This PRD defines product requirements, SKU definitions, SLA tiers, and rollout constraints for the Embedded Runtime consumption offering (embedding Redwood runtime into customer-managed apps and devices). It focuses on creating a predictable consumption model for customers that run the Redwood runtime in constrained environments (edge devices, mobile SDKs, and lightweight on-prem pockets) while preserving our revenue objectives and operational guardrails.

Context and motivators:

- Customers building offline/edge experiences and embedded agents increasingly request a packaged runtime that runs in their environment but connects to Redwood control plane for licensing, telemetry, and optional model fetch.
- Historically Redwood’s hosted and Dedicated SKUs assume our managed GPU fleet and predictable throughput. Embedded runtime changes cost profile: local CPU/GPU variance, intermittent connectivity, and constrained memory.
- To commercialize an Embedded Runtime we need clear, simple SKUs and SLA guarantees the sales and legal teams can contract against, and the platform can instrument and meter.

Goals (what success looks like):

1. Define a compact SKU matrix that maps to expected device classes and fidelity (Low, Standard, High) and to bandwidth/connectivity assumptions.
2. Specify SLA commitments the control plane can provide for telemetry, model delivery, and authentication (not runtime latency guarantees for locally executed tokens).
3. Provide implementation requirements for the runtime (metering hooks, heartbeat, offline usage reconciliation) and the control plane (ingestion, quotas, billing pipeline).
4. Create a rollout plan and migration path from pilot customers to GA with measurable adoption targets.

Non‑goals:

- We are not committing to per-token latency or throughput SLOs for locally executed inference. Those remain customer-managed.
- This PRD does not specify runtime binary packaging formats (that is in ENG-private-deployments).

User personas and primary journeys:

- Embedded App Developer (startup mobile teams):  request simple licensing for local inference binaries, want a small monthly bill predictable by device count and fidelity.
- Platform/IT Buyer (enterprise): negotiate volume SKUs and offline reconciliation windows; expect audit logs and ability to revoke entitlements.
- Field Ops/Integrator: need clear upgrade paths and an ability to throttle model downloads to manage egress costs.

Key assumptions:

- Embedded runtime will ship as a lightweight container/binary with a small agent that reports usage and performs license handshake.
- Customers will accept best-effort model updates; runtime will support pinned model versions and staged rollouts.
- Billing will be primarily subscription-based (per-device / per-seat) optionally metered by tokens for high-fidelity SKUs.

SKU matrix (narrative table):

Each SKU maps to device capabilities and expected fidelity. The table below is textual and intended for the contract language.

- Embedded‑Lite (EL): For devices under 4 CPU cores or <8GB RAM. Low-fidelity models only. Sold per device/month. Defaults: 30 day offline reconciliation, no model auto-update. Control plane telemetry: heartbeat every 24 hours. Price example (list price): $0.50/device/month.
- Embedded‑Edge (EE): For edge servers and phones with 4–8 cores or 8–32GB RAM. Standard fidelity allowed; optional token metering for heavy usage. Sold per device/month with volume discounts. Defaults: 7 day offline reconciliation, staged model updates, telemetry every 6 hours. Price example: $2.50/device/month.
- Embedded‑Pro (EP): For on-prem racks and devices with dedicated accelerators (GPU/NPUs). High fidelity models allowed; hybrid billing: base per-device fee + per-token surcharge for peak usage. Defaults: 24 hour reconciliation, automatic model delta updates, telemetry every hour, and priority model fetch. Price example: $10/device/month + $0.0003/token for tokens above threshold.

SLA commitments (control plane responsibilities):

Redwood will provide the following guarantees associated with the Embedded SKUs. These SLAs are scoped to the control plane features (not local inference quality):

- Licensing and Activation Availability: 99.9% uptime for license validation endpoints measured monthly.
- Model Delivery Service: 99.5% availability for model artifact downloads from Redwood endpoints (customers may configure cached proxies).
- Telemetry Ingestion & Billing Pipeline: 99.0% availability and 24-hour processing window for reconciliation and billing.
- Security & Revocation: We guarantee revocation propagation within 10 minutes for EP, 1 hour for EE, 24 hours for EL.

Telemetry, metering, and offline reconciliation requirements:

- Agent must implement heartbeat, usage delta reporting, and signed reconciliation envelopes. Heartbeat cadence is per SKU default but configurable in customer contracts.
- For devices that go offline beyond reconciliation window, usages are capped at discretion threshold (default: 14 days) and queued; unresolved gaps trigger audit workflow.

API and control plane changes (requirements):

1. New Licensing API endpoints: /v1/embedded/licenses (create, validate, revoke) with JWT-based attestation.
2. Metering endpoints: /v1/embedded/usage-report accepting compressed JSONL envelopes with signed deltas.
3. Model artifact CDN contract: signed manifests and delta patches; control plane must serve manifests with TTL and support range requests.

Security and compliance notes:

- All telemetry must be encrypted in transit and at rest. Optional PII redaction configuration for telemetry.
- EP SKU will integrate with enterprise KMS/HSM for signing model manifests upon request.

Monitoring, observability and success metrics:

Primary metrics to monitor during pilot and GA:

- Weekly active devices per SKU
- Median reconciliation latency (hours)
- Percentage of reconciliations requiring manual audit
- Model delivery success rate (per region)
- License validation latency P95
- Billing pipeline processing lag

Rolling roadmap and milestones (high level):

1. Pilot (Q3 2027): Limited to 3 customers across different device classes. Implement minimal agent telemetry and basic control plane endpoints.
2. Beta (Q4 2027): Expand to 25 customers, add staged model rollout UI in Console, and automated billing backfill.
3. GA (Q1 2028): Public SKUs, partner-ready documentation, pricing published, SDKs and sample apps.

Rollout and migration playbook (contracting + ops):

- Step 1: Pilot agreement signed, provide instrumented runtime and read-only debug access to telemetry.
- Step 2: Run 6-week pilot and collect reconciliation/audit metrics.
- Step 3: Convert to beta contract including updated SKUs and optional token metering. Provide training for Field Ops.
- Step 4: GA enablement: publish pricing, enable signup flow, and migrate early beta customers to standard billing.

Billing and collections notes:

- Billing will support subscription invoices and token-based surcharges for EP customers.
- Offline reconciliation edge case: usage credits may be withheld if reconciliation exceeds contractual window without justification.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: Customers will place undue latency expectations on local inference; mitigation: documentation and contract language explicitly separate control plane SLAs from local inference performance.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps from long offline windows create billing disputes; mitigation: reconciliation window, signed envelopes, and a human-first audit escalation path.
- Risk: Model artifact distribution loads may spike in regional incidents; mitigation: CDN auto-fallback and customer-configurable cache proxies.

Open questions and decisions needed (for product steering committee):

1. Should EL include any per-token metering at all, or strictly per-device subscription? (Recommend: subscription-only to keep price simple.)
2. Revocation windows and enforcement: default values are in this doc but need legal sign-off for contractual language.
3. Pricing: list prices above are initial guidance; Sales to return target discounting bands and enterprise uplift.

Ownership and next steps:

- Product owner: Maya Chen (product)
- Engineering lead: Owen Patel (eng-private-deployments)
- Security reviewer: Priya Rao (security)
